name: Design a workflow as a process map: messy prototype, then clean final map
goal: Design or document a workflow by mapping it as a process map (inputs, ordered steps, decisions, stakeholders, outputs): start with a messy prototype map of the one process causing the most pain, share and iterate, then publish a clean final documentation map and keep it updated.

source.title: Business Process Mapping 101 (Step By Step Guide)
source.transcript_note: Auto-generated English track, same as Show transcript.

prerequisites: A process to map (one that currently bothers you most)
Pen and paper, whiteboard, sticky notes, or a diagram tool (Lucidchart or Miro named in the video)

inputs.name: process
inputs.description: The workflow to design, e.g. client onboarding, sales, or a song-production pipeline

outputs.name: prototype_map
outputs.description: Messy map of current state plus possible improvements, notes, links, screenshots

outputs.name: final_map
outputs.description: Clean as-is blueprint: ordered boxes, decisions, parallel flows, final output; no what-ifs

constraints: Do not wait for the perfect tool or full detail; a v1 on paper is the goal (avoid analysis paralysis).
Map one process per map/tab; a larger system is a collection of separate maps.
The prototype map may hold current state and future ideas; the final map shows only what currently happens.
Share the map early, even as a photo; collaboration is the point.
A process map is a living document; revisit and update it as the process changes.
Written SOPs come after the map, as detail layered onto it.

steps.action: Pick the single process that is currently causing the most trouble; skip choosing tools or depth for now.
steps.expect: One named process with a clear end output

steps.action: On paper/whiteboard/sticky notes, write the steps as simple boxes in sequential order (this, then this, then this, then the final output), noting inputs, decision points, and who is involved.
Expand it into a prototype map with collaborators: add context, links to tools, screenshots, problems, and improvement ideas without worrying about looks.
steps.expect: Messy map showing current state and possible future states

steps.action: Share it (photo or link), walk someone through it, collect comments, and iterate.
Produce the final documentation map: only the as-is steps in order, decisions and parallel flows from trigger to final output, with notes and clutter removed.
steps.expect: Concise blueprint someone can follow day to day

steps.action: Move it into a shareable tool with access controls if needed, one tab per subprocess, and optionally add detailed docs/SOPs that expand each box.
steps.expect: Organised set of maps (the video's 'company brain')

steps.action: Revisit the map whenever the process changes or a better way is found, and update it.

verification: Final map has a clear start trigger, ordered steps, any decision points, and a single final output
Final map contains no future/what-if notes
At least one other person/agent has reviewed the map
